title: Bias-Corrected Multi-Factor Pipeline for H198: Mask-First Design and Alpha101 Factor Engineering
source: arXiv:2507.07107 (Du, May 2026) — "Machine Learning Enhanced Multi-Factor Quantitative Trading: A Cross-Sectional Portfolio Optimization Approach with Bias Correction"
summary: Du identifies 'upstream contamination' in rolling factor pipelines: non-tradable days (thin volume, halts, earnings blackout windows) silently propagate into downstream moving averages and ranks, inflating apparent IC by ~18% while reducing realized Sharpe by 0.44 points. The fix is a mask-first design: construct a tradability mask from volume data at load time and thread it through every operator so no window reads a non-tradable price. H460 applies this to H198: (1) build a daily volume mask (days where any stock in H198 universe trades < 20th percentile volume = suspect), (2) recompute 6-1m momentum and IMOM signals with mask applied, (3) additionally test a curated set of Alpha101 factors that survive the bias-correction filter on US large-cap data. Gate: if masked momentum OOS Sharpe > unmasked baseline, record as bias-corrected champion.
variants: Var A: Mask-corrected 6-1m momentum top-6 (volume mask at 20th pct threshold)
Var B: Mask-corrected 6-1m momentum top-6 (volume mask at 10th pct threshold, stricter)
Var C: Mask-corrected IMOM6 signal top-6 (illusion momentum with contamination removed)
Var D: Alpha101 factor #001 (1-day reversal) with mask — cross-sectional test on H198
Var E: H198 baseline unmasked 6-1m momentum top-6 (sanity check)
gate: OOS Sharpe >= 1.174 (H198 baseline) — any improvement in Sharpe or MaxDD via masking is informative
